pathway.title: Qnity Electronics, Inc. — Credit Snapshot
pathway.question: Should we own this issuer, in which instrument, and why?

runs.text: First, leverage fell and liquidity is ample. Qnity Electronics, Inc. reports total debt of USD 4,019 million against cash of USD 1,124 million and a fully undrawn USD 1,250 million revolver (USD 1,238 million after letters of credit), so liquidity is USD 2,362 million [CP-1]. Total debt to LTM Adjusted Operating EBITDA is 2.37x, down from 2.79x at FY2025, and net debt to EBITDA is 1.71x against 2.16x. Debt maturities are USD 24 million a year to 2030 and USD 3,980 million after that, so the notes and term loan fall due in 2032 and 2033, beyond the revolver's October 2030 expiry. The mechanism is that EBITDA grew while debt was little changed; the implication is low near-term refinancing risk and a cushion against an earnings shortfall.

Second, the adjusted measures overstate cash available for creditors. For nine months 2026, operating cash flow less capex was USD 357 million, against company adjusted free cash flow of USD 607 million; the USD 250 million difference is transformation cash costs, indirect legacy payments to DuPont and a separation foreign tax cost [CP-1]. Qnity also paid USD 125 million in dividends and buybacks in the same period. Debt reduction therefore depends on cash that is smaller than adjusted figures show and is shared with shareholders, with the restricted payment baskets not known.

Third, revenue visibility is short. Customer contracts carry no long-term purchase commitments, the top ten customers were 34% of 2025 net sales, and most sales are in Asia Pacific [CP-1A]. Growth in 2026 has been primarily volume, attributed by management to AI-driven demand. A cut in orders by one large customer would reach earnings quickly through lost absorption, and leverage is sensitive to that: LTM Adjusted Operating EBITDA would have to fall 21.0% for total debt to reach 3.0x and 32.3% to reach 3.5x (illustrative thresholds, not covenants).

Fourth, claims outside debt are material and growing. Qnity bears 44% of certain DuPont legacy liabilities, including PFAS settlements; the 10-Q states exposure could be up to about USD 100 million above the amount accrued, and a new North Carolina settlement added to the accrual in 2026 [CP-1, CP-1A]. The Tax Matters Agreement can add tax indemnities if the spin-off fails to qualify as tax-free. These are senior-ranking cash claims that sit outside the debt figure.

Fifth, interest is a new and partly floating cost. Interest expense was USD 237 million over the last twelve months and USD 64 million in Q3 2026, so LTM Adjusted Operating EBITDA covers annualised latest-quarter interest 6.62x and LTM interest expense 7.15x [CP-1]. The term loan carries a variable rate, and the annual report states that a 100 basis point change would move annual interest expense by USD 24 million (K p:82); no hedge is reported in the pinned filings. Cash interest paid is not printed for 2026, so a cash-basis cover ratio cannot be built.

Sixth, the capital structure came from the separation. The term loan and note proceeds were paid to DuPont as a cash dividend, and Qnity had no independent board while the separation agreements were negotiated [CP-1A]. There is no sponsor, and no creditor-adverse transaction is documented since; the July 2026 repricing lowered the borrowing margin without changing security or maturity. Capacity to make distributions or incur debt cannot be tested because the credit agreement and indentures are not supplied.

runs.text: Strengths. Qnity Electronics, Inc. has moderate and falling leverage: total debt to LTM Adjusted Operating EBITDA is 2.37x and net debt to EBITDA is 1.71x [CP-1; Documentary Fact from a CP-1 figure]. It has deep liquidity of USD 2,362 million, with no committed facility expiring within twelve months and USD 785 million of its USD 1,124 million cash held in foreign subsidiaries, which may limit how much is freely available in the United States [CP-1; Documentary Fact]. Its debt is long-dated, with scheduled amortisation of about USD 24 million a year and the notes and term loan due in 2032 and 2033 [CP-1; Documentary Fact]. Its operating base is growing on volume in both segments, with an LTM Adjusted Operating EBITDA margin of 30.9% on USD 5,490 million of LTM net sales [CP-1, CP-1A; Documentary Fact, with the margin a company measure]. Its products are consumables, over 90% of 2025 revenue came from products used in manufacturing or incorporated in devices, and about 70% of raw materials are sourced locally with no supplier above 10% of raw material spend, which reduces input and tariff risk [CP-1A; Documentary Fact]. There is no sponsor and no documented creditor-adverse act since the separation [CP-1A; Analyst Interpretation].

Weaknesses. Demand is concentrated and cancellable: the top ten customers were 34% of 2025 net sales, two named customers were about a tenth of sales each in 2026, and contracts carry no long-term purchase commitments [CP-1A; Documentary Fact]. Adjusted Operating EBITDA excludes real cash costs, so operating cash flow less capex of USD 357 million trails company adjusted free cash flow of USD 607 million for nine months 2026 [CP-1; Documentary Fact from CP-1 figures]. Claims outside debt include a 44% share of DuPont legacy liabilities, tax indemnities and operating leases of USD 514 million, and the legacy exposure is not capped [CP-1, CP-1A; Documentary Fact]. Shareholder returns of USD 125 million over nine months, with USD 425 million of repurchase authorization remaining, compete with debt reduction [CP-1; Documentary Fact]. The term loan is floating-rate and no hedge is reported, so a 100 basis point move changes interest expense by USD 24 million a year [K p:82; Documentary Fact, added here]. Qnity has about eleven months of stand-alone results at September 30, 2026, so the trend in interest, tax and cost lines is not like-for-like with the carve-out periods [CP-0, CP-1; Analyst Interpretation]. Management's descriptions of itself as the premier provider and of consecutive profitable growth are Management Language and are not adopted [CP-1A].

blocks.title: Transaction summary and new debt issues

runs.text: The defining transaction is the separation of Qnity from DuPont de Nemours, Inc., announced on May 22, 2024 and completed on November 1, 2025 by a pro-rata distribution of one Qnity share for every two DuPont shares held on the record date of October 22, 2025 (K p:6). Qnity common stock began trading on the New York Stock Exchange on November 3, 2025. There is no sponsor and no change-of-control transaction in the sources, and no acquisition or disposal of a business is reported in the 2026 filings read for this module. The annual report states that Qnity may pursue bolt-on and strategic acquisitions (K p:17), which is intent, not an event.

New debt was raised in two steps before the distribution. On August 15, 2025 the issuer sold senior secured notes due 2032 and senior unsecured notes due 2033, each guaranteed by every subsidiary that is a borrower or guarantor under the credit facilities, with the secured notes sharing first-priority liens pari passu with the credit facilities (K p:116 to p:118). On October 31, 2025 it entered a credit agreement for a seven-year term loan and a five-year revolving facility, and the annual report states that the full term loan, together with the notes proceeds, was paid directly to DuPont as a cash dividend in connection with the separation (K p:119). The aggregate principal incurred in connection with the spin-off is stated as 4.1 billion (K p:43), and the financial base handoff carries the instrument-level terms, the maturities and the liquidity position. The use of proceeds is therefore a documented distribution to the former parent, recorded in the cash flow statement as net transfers to the parent. This is a debt-funded distribution at separation, made when the parent still controlled the subsidiary and set its terms; the annual report states Qnity had no independent board or management team representing its interests while the separation agreements were negotiated (K p:45).

Since the distribution the documented actions are a quarterly dividend, a share repurchase authorization, a repricing of the term loan and scheduled amortization. The repricing, effective July 1, 2026, cut the margin on term SOFR borrowings from 2.00% to 1.75% with no material change to principal, maturity, amortization or covenant structure, and carries a 1.00% premium on repricing events for six months (Q3 p:20); it is a borrower-favourable amendment to a creditor-owned instrument, not a creditor-adverse one. The amendment document itself is not supplied. Liquidity effect: the financial base shows an undrawn revolver and cash, with no facility expiring within twelve months. Status of every transaction item is final and closed; the only open items are contingent legacy payments to DuPont described under governance below.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The reported-fact base is adequate to underwrite a first view, and it is cleaner than the carve-out history suggests because the standalone capital structure has been in place since November 1, 2025. On filed figures, net sales were 4,300 for nine months 2026 against 3,564 a year earlier, and Adjusted Operating EBITDA was 1,345 against 1,091. Total debt of 4,019 at September 30, 2026 compares with 1,124 of cash and a fully undrawn 1,250 revolver (1,238 after letters of credit). Calculated leverage is 2.37x total and 1.71x net on LTM Adjusted Operating EBITDA, down from 2.79x and 2.16x at FY2025. Three points temper this. First, the EBITDA measure excludes indirect legacy costs (84 in nine months 2026) and transformation, integration and other charges (123), which are real cash outflows. Second, interest cover on LTM interest expense flatters the run rate, because the LTM window includes a quarter in which the term loan was outstanding for only two months. Third, FY2025 and nine months 2025 are carve-out periods, so year-on-year changes in interest, tax and allocated costs mix a basis change with performance. The covenant headroom cannot be read from the sources: the maintenance test and its level are disclosed, the issuer's reported ratio and its covenant EBITDA definition are not.

fields.value: Qnity Electronics, Inc. is a Delaware-incorporated supplier of consumable materials to semiconductor fabrication and to electronics interconnect, reported in two segments, Semiconductor Technologies and Interconnect Solutions. It became independent on November 1, 2025 through a pro-rata distribution by DuPont de Nemours, Inc., and its shares have traded on the New York Stock Exchange since November 3, 2025. The credit-relevant structure is a stand-alone, widely held company with no sponsor, whose debt was raised just before the distribution, at the issuer level with subsidiary guarantees, and was paid out to the former parent. The debt amount was set in connection with the separation. Operating strength is evident in the filings: volume-led sales growth in both segments, driven by AI-linked demand in advanced nodes, advanced packaging and thermal management, and a consumable revenue model. Two features constrain the creditor view. First, customer contracts carry no long-term purchase commitments and the top ten customers are concentrated, so revenue visibility rests on customer forecasts that can be cancelled. Second, Qnity has contractually taken on a share of DuPont's legacy liabilities and some tax exposure under agreements negotiated before it had an independent board. Post-separation behaviour is documented as a quarterly dividend, a share repurchase programme, a borrower-favourable term loan repricing and debt amortization. No document shows priming, uptiering, drop-downs or collateral release. Missing is any executed document or management presentation, so terms and management's own capital allocation priorities are visible only through filing summaries.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The defining transaction is the separation of Qnity from DuPont de Nemours, Inc., announced on May 22, 2024 and completed on November 1, 2025 by a pro-rata distribution of one Qnity share for every two DuPont shares held on the record date of October 22, 2025 (K p:6). Qnity common stock began trading on the New York Stock Exchange on November 3, 2025. There is no sponsor and no change-of-control transaction in the sources, and no acquisition or disposal of a business is reported in the 2026 filings read for this module. The annual report states that Qnity may pursue bolt-on and strategic acquisitions (K p:17), which is intent, not an event.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: New debt was raised in two steps before the distribution. On August 15, 2025 the issuer sold senior secured notes due 2032 and senior unsecured notes due 2033, each guaranteed by every subsidiary that is a borrower or guarantor under the credit facilities, with the secured notes sharing first-priority liens pari passu with the credit facilities (K p:116 to p:118). On October 31, 2025 it entered a credit agreement for a seven-year term loan and a five-year revolving facility, and the annual report states that the full term loan, together with the notes proceeds, was paid directly to DuPont as a cash dividend in connection with the separation (K p:119). The aggregate principal incurred in connection with the spin-off is stated as 4.1 billion (K p:43), and the financial base handoff carries the instrument-level terms, the maturities and the liquidity position. The use of proceeds is therefore a documented distribution to the former parent, recorded in the cash flow statement as net transfers to the parent. This is a debt-funded distribution at separation, made when the parent still controlled the subsidiary and set its terms; the annual report states Qnity had no independent board or management team representing its interests while the separation agreements were negotiated (K p:45).

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Since the distribution the documented actions are a quarterly dividend, a share repurchase authorization, a repricing of the term loan and scheduled amortization. The repricing, effective July 1, 2026, cut the margin on term SOFR borrowings from 2.00% to 1.75% with no material change to principal, maturity, amortization or covenant structure, and carries a 1.00% premium on repricing events for six months (Q3 p:20); it is a borrower-favourable amendment to a creditor-owned instrument, not a creditor-adverse one. The amendment document itself is not supplied. Liquidity effect: the financial base shows an undrawn revolver and cash, with no facility expiring within twelve months. Status of every transaction item is final and closed; the only open items are contingent legacy payments to DuPont described under governance below.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Qnity Electronics, Inc. has a moderate-leverage, well-funded credit profile with earnings quality that is weaker than the headline ratios suggest. The strongest support is financial: total debt of USD 4,019 million is 2.37x LTM Adjusted Operating EBITDA, liquidity is USD 2,362 million, the revolver is undrawn to October 2030 and no large maturity falls before 2032. The weakest point is the durability of the cash behind those ratios. Demand is volume-driven, cancellable and concentrated in a few customers, adjusted EBITDA leaves out legacy and transformation cash costs, and a 44% share of DuPont legacy liabilities sits outside debt. The outcome will be decided by whether AI-linked volume growth persists while cash after interest, legacy payments and shareholder returns keeps reducing leverage. Covenant headroom cannot be verified from the sources.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: First, leverage fell and liquidity is ample. Qnity Electronics, Inc. reports total debt of USD 4,019 million against cash of USD 1,124 million and a fully undrawn USD 1,250 million revolver (USD 1,238 million after letters of credit), so liquidity is USD 2,362 million [CP-1]. Total debt to LTM Adjusted Operating EBITDA is 2.37x, down from 2.79x at FY2025, and net debt to EBITDA is 1.71x against 2.16x. Debt maturities are USD 24 million a year to 2030 and USD 3,980 million after that, so the notes and term loan fall due in 2032 and 2033, beyond the revolver's October 2030 expiry. The mechanism is that EBITDA grew while debt was little changed; the implication is low near-term refinancing risk and a cushion against an earnings shortfall.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Second, the adjusted measures overstate cash available for creditors. For nine months 2026, operating cash flow less capex was USD 357 million, against company adjusted free cash flow of USD 607 million; the USD 250 million difference is transformation cash costs, indirect legacy payments to DuPont and a separation foreign tax cost [CP-1]. Qnity also paid USD 125 million in dividends and buybacks in the same period. Debt reduction therefore depends on cash that is smaller than adjusted figures show and is shared with shareholders, with the restricted payment baskets not known.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Third, revenue visibility is short. Customer contracts carry no long-term purchase commitments, the top ten customers were 34% of 2025 net sales, and most sales are in Asia Pacific [CP-1A]. Growth in 2026 has been primarily volume, attributed by management to AI-driven demand. A cut in orders by one large customer would reach earnings quickly through lost absorption, and leverage is sensitive to that: LTM Adjusted Operating EBITDA would have to fall 21.0% for total debt to reach 3.0x and 32.3% to reach 3.5x (illustrative thresholds, not covenants).

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Fourth, claims outside debt are material and growing. Qnity bears 44% of certain DuPont legacy liabilities, including PFAS settlements; the 10-Q states exposure could be up to about USD 100 million above the amount accrued, and a new North Carolina settlement added to the accrual in 2026 [CP-1, CP-1A]. The Tax Matters Agreement can add tax indemnities if the spin-off fails to qualify as tax-free. These are senior-ranking cash claims that sit outside the debt figure.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Fifth, interest is a new and partly floating cost. Interest expense was USD 237 million over the last twelve months and USD 64 million in Q3 2026, so LTM Adjusted Operating EBITDA covers annualised latest-quarter interest 6.62x and LTM interest expense 7.15x [CP-1]. The term loan carries a variable rate, and the annual report states that a 100 basis point change would move annual interest expense by USD 24 million (K p:82); no hedge is reported in the pinned filings. Cash interest paid is not printed for 2026, so a cash-basis cover ratio cannot be built.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Sixth, the capital structure came from the separation. The term loan and note proceeds were paid to DuPont as a cash dividend, and Qnity had no independent board while the separation agreements were negotiated [CP-1A]. There is no sponsor, and no creditor-adverse transaction is documented since; the July 2026 repricing lowered the borrowing margin without changing security or maturity. Capacity to make distributions or incur debt cannot be tested because the credit agreement and indentures are not supplied.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Strengths. Qnity Electronics, Inc. has moderate and falling leverage: total debt to LTM Adjusted Operating EBITDA is 2.37x and net debt to EBITDA is 1.71x [CP-1; Documentary Fact from a CP-1 figure]. It has deep liquidity of USD 2,362 million, with no committed facility expiring within twelve months and USD 785 million of its USD 1,124 million cash held in foreign subsidiaries, which may limit how much is freely available in the United States [CP-1; Documentary Fact]. Its debt is long-dated, with scheduled amortisation of about USD 24 million a year and the notes and term loan due in 2032 and 2033 [CP-1; Documentary Fact]. Its operating base is growing on volume in both segments, with an LTM Adjusted Operating EBITDA margin of 30.9% on USD 5,490 million of LTM net sales [CP-1, CP-1A; Documentary Fact, with the margin a company measure]. Its products are consumables, over 90% of 2025 revenue came from products used in manufacturing or incorporated in devices, and about 70% of raw materials are sourced locally with no supplier above 10% of raw material spend, which reduces input and tariff risk [CP-1A; Documentary Fact]. There is no sponsor and no documented creditor-adverse act since the separation [CP-1A; Analyst Interpretation].

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Weaknesses. Demand is concentrated and cancellable: the top ten customers were 34% of 2025 net sales, two named customers were about a tenth of sales each in 2026, and contracts carry no long-term purchase commitments [CP-1A; Documentary Fact]. Adjusted Operating EBITDA excludes real cash costs, so operating cash flow less capex of USD 357 million trails company adjusted free cash flow of USD 607 million for nine months 2026 [CP-1; Documentary Fact from CP-1 figures]. Claims outside debt include a 44% share of DuPont legacy liabilities, tax indemnities and operating leases of USD 514 million, and the legacy exposure is not capped [CP-1, CP-1A; Documentary Fact]. Shareholder returns of USD 125 million over nine months, with USD 425 million of repurchase authorization remaining, compete with debt reduction [CP-1; Documentary Fact]. The term loan is floating-rate and no hedge is reported, so a 100 basis point move changes interest expense by USD 24 million a year [K p:82; Documentary Fact, added here]. Qnity has about eleven months of stand-alone results at September 30, 2026, so the trend in interest, tax and cost lines is not like-for-like with the carve-out periods [CP-0, CP-1; Analyst Interpretation]. Management's descriptions of itself as the premier provider and of consecutive profitable growth are Management Language and are not adopted [CP-1A].
